PER-CRITERION. C1 MET -- I read the live schema myself: published_at TIMESTAMP REQUIRED and a distinct ingested_at TIMESTAMP REQUIRED, fetched_at gone; my q10 mutant (live read returns a schema with fetched_at restored and provenance NULLABLE) turns C1 RED, so the guard can fail when its subject is broken. C2 MET -- provenance STRING REQUIRED in BOTH tables (live read by me); live/backfill discrimination is now mutation-proven at THREE seams: the article path (q1, q8 killed), the sentiment write seam (m7, q5 killed) and the e2e pipeline (m8, m9, q6 killed), and confirmed compositionally by my real-pipeline probe. C3 MET -- both halves (strict counter increase AND a WARNING log record) asserted in one test while the writer returns 0 without raising; two negative controls (successful write, empty input) present; q2 kills it. C4 MET -- the assertion is `after == before + 1`, a strict numeric increase, not attribute existence; deleting the increment (q2) and the author's `+1 -> +0` (m3) both kill. C5 MET -- two distinct registered adapters flow through the writer, and the import-chain scan is proven non-tautological by known-member recall against the REAL backend/tools/alphavantage.py. C6 MET -- independently re-derived, empty diff over exactly the two adapter paths plus a clean git status in backend/news/sources/.

TWO SURVIVING MUTANTS -- both NOTE-level, neither a criterion miss, each with a named fix.
(a) q3: aliasing `_serialize_article`'s `ingested_at` to `article.get("published_at")` -- collapsing the two column VALUES in every written row -- leaves all 11 tests green. Behavioural differential is real, but criterion 1 is worded at the SCHEMA/column-name level ("if the two resolve to the same column NAME"), so row-value distinctness is outside it; and the shipped behaviour is correct -- my runtime smoke shows published_at != ingested_at on all 3 live-produced articles. A value-distinctness guard would also be entangled today with the queued 83.0.1 defect (fetcher stamps published_at with the wall clock when absent), which the author correctly scoped out with an in-code comment. Named fix: add a row-level assertion once 83.0.1 lands.
(b) q4: forcing `bigquery.Client.get_table` to raise 404 -- exactly the pre-migration state -- also leaves all 11 green, because `_resolve_schema`'s `except Exception: pass` silently substitutes the checked-in snapshot. So in a credential-less runner the C1/C2 schema assertions degrade to self-attestation. This does NOT bite here: my complementary q7 (blanking the snapshot while live BQ is reachable) also survives, proving the LIVE branch is what fed the assertions on this rig, and q10 proves that branch is load-bearing; the fallback is disclosed in the test docstring; and the migration's own verify_post_condition() plus the live_check BEFORE/AFTER captures cover the real event. Named fix: skip/xfail when BQ is unreachable instead of silently substituting. Recorded as a reusable vacuity shape in my agent memory.

CARRIED-FORWARD NOTES from cycle 2, still true, still non-blocking: `_serialize_article`/`_serialize_sentiment` coerce an invalid provenance to "live" -- the more dangerous of the two values -- and BQ has no CHECK constraints, so "unknown" or a recorded failure would be safer; and the 9 stub rows now in prod carry provenance='live', which is itself untrue for a synthetic row (the two-value enum has no slot for it). 83.0.7 covers their purge.

SCOPE HONESTY: high, and it improved under pressure. The author disclosed the corrected 12 -> 11 test count against the measured run; disclosed that mutant m6's first formulation SURVIVED and was reformulated; disclosed the stub-row pollution incident with a $0 cost derivation and queued it as 83.0.7; queued the disjoint live news path (83.0.4) and the absent api_call_log table (83.0.5); and preserved the false D1 sentence verbatim under a Correction heading rather than quietly editing it. I found no overclaim: every number in experiment_results_83.0.md that I re-derived (11 passed, 22 passed, 6-file lint scope, empty adapter diff, 80/0 masterplan numstat, 9/9 mutants) reproduced.

CODE-REVIEW HEURISTICS (5 dimensions): no BLOCK, no WARN. No secret in the diff; the only subprocess call is a literal git argv list inside a test (shell=False); no prompt-injection or LLM-output-to-execution path. Trading domain: no kill_switch, stop-loss, perf_metrics, position-sizing or paper_trader path touched. bq-schema-migration-safety does NOT fire -- both tables were CREATED fresh, not altered, which is provable rather than asserted: BigQuery forbids adding a REQUIRED column to an existing table, so a live REQUIRED `provenance` on both tables can only have come from this CREATE. consumer-contract-break does not fire: `run_once(..., provenance="live")`, `_normalize(..., provenance=)`, `write_news_sentiment(..., provenance=None)` and `_serialize_sentiment(result, default_provenance=None)` are all purely ADDITIVE defaulted kwargs (negation-list exempt), and I grepped the consumers -- the only non-test caller is phase6_e2e, updated in the same diff. The pre-existing fail-open `except Exception` in `_insert_rows` is now instrumented with a counter plus WARNING, a strict improvement on the swallowed-warning baseline, which is why paper-trader-broad-except does not fire.

EVIDENCE PROVENANCE: every piece of live evidence in this verdict was captured BY ME -- the three BQ schema reads, all pytest runs, the ruff run, all 11 mutation injections, the real-pipeline probe, the known-member recall test, and every git derivation. All mutations ran in-process via sys.modules and attribute injection and the probe neutralized bq_writer._insert_rows, so there were ZERO repo writes and ZERO BigQuery writes from my evaluation and nothing needed restoring. I deliberately did NOT run scripts/smoketest/phase6_e2e.py as a script, because doing so writes to production BigQuery -- that is precisely the 83.0.7 incident. The qa-write-guard hook correctly blocked my one attempt to stage a scratchpad helper; I moved the harness to stdin, which is the right pattern for a read-only evaluator.

RESIDUAL RISK FOR THE OPERATOR (not blocking, already queued): the corpus this step makes writable is still DISJOINT from the news path that actually moves the live book (news_screen.py -> screener.py:334), so 83.0 delivers the schema prerequisite and the audit trail, not the capture of market-moving headlines. 83.0.4 is the step that closes that gap, and it should be treated as the one with money value. The 9 stub rows sitting in the streaming buffer under provenance='live' are a small but real integrity blemish on a brand-new audit table -- 83.0.7 should run before anyone queries these tables for a point-in-time claim.
